Dear Mr. Robein: providers of continuing education.
Our office received an opinion request from you submitted as counsel for the Louisiana
State Plumbing Board (“LSPB”) concerning whether the LSPB may offer continuing
professional education classes to licensed plumbers to fulfill the continuing education
requirement set by the LSPB.
As described in La. R.S. 37:1361(A):
The purpose of the legislature in enacting this Chapter is the protection of
the health, safety, environment, and general welfare of all those persons
who use and rely upon plumbing, and medical gas and vacuum systems
for their personal or commercial needs, and the affording to such persons
of an effective and practical protection against incompetent,
inexperienced, or unlawful acts by persons who perform plumbing and
medical gas and vacuum systems work. Further, the legislative intent is
that the State Plumbing Board shall be the sole and exclusive agency in
this state empowered to license natural persons and regulated business
entities engaged or seeking to engage in the business of plumbing and
medical gas and vacuum systems installation and verification and to
ensure compliance with the licensing requirements of this Chapter.
Nothing herein shall preclude any current authority of the State Licensing
Board for Contractors.
Consistent with the above described statute, the LSPB is authorized to formulate and
promulgate rules and regulations to govern the plumbing profession. Chapter 16 of Title
37 of the Revised Statutes addresses the rulemaking authority of the LSPB with respect
to continuing professional development, La. R.S. 37:1366(I) providing: “[t]he board may
establish and determine by rule minimum requirements relative to continuing
professional development for the renewal or reinstatement of any license or special

endorsement issued by the board.” The LSPB promulgated rules which establish a
program of continuing professional education (“CPE”), outlining specific CPE hours
which must be obtained by active plumbers seeking to renew a journeyman or master
plumber’s license (LAC 46:LV.1001),1 a water supply protection specialist endorsement
(LAC 46:LV.1003), and/or a medical gas piping installer or medical gas verifier license
(LAC 46:LV.1005).
In general, the rules describe: the number of CPE hours required for renewal;2 course
material which must be submitted to the LSPB annually for approval;3 course form and
content requirements;4 course provider requirements;5 and course instructor
requirements.6 Further, LAC 46:LV.1001(C)(10) specifically acknowledges the authority
of the LSPB to enter into a cooperative endeavor with certain groups to jointly provide
CPE services to licensed journeyman and master plumbers.7
The question submitted to this office for consideration in this opinion request is whether
the LSPB itself may offer CPE courses to fulfill the CPE requirements set and approved
by the LSPB. As described by La. R.S. 37:1361(A), the purpose behind the statutes
regulating the licensing of plumbers is the protection of the health, safety, environment
and general welfare of all persons who use and rely upon plumbing, and medical gas
and vacuum systems for personal or commercial needs, and to afford such persons an
effective and practical protection against incompetent, inexperienced, or unlawful acts
by persons who perform plumbing, and medical gas and vacuum systems work.
Further, as described by La. R.S. 37:1366(I), the legislature has specifically authorized
the LSPB to establish and determine minimum requirements relative to continuing
professional development of individuals who have received a license or special
endorsement issued by the LSPB. It would fit within this statutory authority for the
LSPB to provide CPE courses to fulfill CPE requirements set by the LSPB. Of course,
any classes sponsored by the LSPB would be subject to the substantive and procedural
requirements set forth in the rules promulgated by the LSPB, including the approval
process for providers of continuing education.
This conclusion is consistent with previous opinions issued by this office, where we
have stated the Louisiana Board of Examiners of Certified Shorthand Reporters may
sponsor continuing education courses (La. Atty. Gen. Op. No. 10-0084) and the Board

United States or its agencies, or with any public or private association, corporation, or individual.”

OPINION 13-0083
63 – B – LICENSING – For professions or occupations
La. R.S. 37:1361
La. R.S. 37:1366
The Louisiana State Plumbing Board (“LSPB”) may offer continuing professional
education courses to fulfill the requirements set and approved by the LSPB. Any
classes sponsored by the LSPB would be subject to the substantive and procedural
requirements set forth in the rules promulgated by the LSPB, including the approval
process for providers of continuing education.
